A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, references, and appendices support comparison, including matching material relocated between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative video-generation comparisons, qualitative examples, and component ablations in Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds LongLive comparisons, 60-second generation results, and a 31-participant user study.

M1.justification: The shared encoder, separate flow-matching and distribution-matching heads, training objectives, and few-step inference procedure remain unchanged. The sliding-window latent reconstruction procedure in v2 Section 3.4 was already documented in v1 Appendix C.

E1.justification: v2 adds a 60-second generation scenario requiring sustained coherence beyond the retained 30-second evaluation. The training sources—Sekai, MiraData, and collected internet videos—and the underlying text-to-video task remain unchanged.

E2.justification: LongLive is added as an evaluated comparator in Table 1 and Figure 4; v1 cited it but did not include it in those comparisons. All previously evaluated comparators remain.

E3.justification: Appendix C introduces a human-evaluation protocol: 31 participants view randomized sets, comprising 25 sets at 30 seconds and 15 at 60 seconds, and rate quality, consistency, and static artifacts. Appendix B adds 60-second automatic evaluation restricted to available rollout/context-extension baselines. The original 200-prompt, 30-second evaluation remains unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 2 remain unchanged. Appendix B adds a focused horizon stress test examining whether fidelity and temporal evolution persist at 60 seconds, while the user study supplies targeted static-artifact ratings relevant to motion collapse.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without generation seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2's participant count and averaged human ratings describe the new study rather than introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All existing numerical entries in Tables 1–2 are unchanged, but Table 1 gains LongLive results. New Table 3 reports 60-second outcomes, including 0.9297 dynamic degree and 73.08 VLM consistency for the proposed method. Table 4 adds human ratings showing its highest overall quality and global consistency at both horizons. These are additional results, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives and numbered equations remain unchanged. Section 3.3 expresses the existing conditional-mean versus mode-seeking motivation using explicit optimum notation and explanatory qualifications, without adding a substantive derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain sliding-window teacher alignment, decoupled global/local training heads, and fast long-video generation. The abstract now names human ratings and one-minute tests as supporting evidence, but retains the same scientific claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds concrete limitations involving action-state transitions and landmark revisitation, motivating stronger event planning and memory. It also qualifies the incomplete 60-second baseline coverage and cautions that LongLive's NFE is not directly comparable. The original interpretations of SFT, teacher alignment, and their combination remain.

D1.justification: Hardware, batching, sequence-parallelism settings, data preparation, and latent-boundary handling are retained and relocated into the main text. However, v2 omits the direct FastGen repository URL supplied in v1's references, while retaining the named codebase and project website; this slightly reduces access information.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a substantial diffusion-distillation discussion covering trajectory regression, consistency methods, distribution matching, and hybrids. It explicitly positions the proposed global/local objective separation against approaches blending objectives on one output. Publication-year and title updates to retained references do not constitute additional research changes.

P1.justification: v2 moves v1 Appendices A–C into Sections 4.1 and 3.4, reorganizes the remaining appendices, expands the mean-versus-mode explanation, and removes the duplicated contribution-introduction sentence. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial tables for one-minute results and human ratings. Figure 4 is reorganized from two to three frames per scene and gains a LongLive row; Table 1 also gains that comparator and an expanded caption. Figures 1–3 and the ablation display are substantially retained.

improvement.justification: v1's minute-scale claims relied mainly on 30-second automatic evaluation. v2 directly strengthens their empirical basis with 60-second results and human judgments of quality, consistency, and static artifacts, while adding concrete planning limitations. This substantially improves validation and qualification of the central contribution. The longer-horizon comparison still lacks SFT-only baselines, and the human ratings lack uncertainty estimates, limiting the strength of comparative conclusions.
